name: Willis Towers Watson Public Limited Company
moat_justification: Scale global broker/adviser with high client retention, embedded relationships and data/analytics, but it is the #3 player behind Marsh McLennan and Aon, the assets walk out the door (brokers/consultants), and a softening insurance pricing cycle plus AI-enabled challengers pressure the model.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 4.0%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.8x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Good asset-light broker/adviser, moat 6/10 — but at $297.15 it does not clear 15% (9.8% weighted IRR, IV@15 $167.08); it would need to fall to about $167 to clear the hurdle.
moat_for: Global scale and network for multinational clients
High retention and switching friction in embedded benefits/retirement and broking relationships
Data, analytics and specialty expertise (climate, cyber, M&A, specialty lines)
Asset-light recurring fee model with buyback-funded per-share compounding
moat_against: #3 scale position behind Marsh McLennan and Aon; Gallagher consolidating the middle market
People are the asset — producer/consultant poaching is a permanent erosion force
Softening insurance pricing cycle is a direct headwind to brokerage commissions
AI/automation and tech-native brokers can compress middle-market broking economics
